summary: Lena finds and reads the diary's open first page. "A child’s hand had written, across a space like a breath: \"Hush, the sea will sing you home.\"" Source: s-001 (.writer/drafts/s-001.md; .context-builder/history/ch-01/s-001.md).
Lena opens the cedar trunk; its lid bore a yellowing sticker reading exactly: "May Harper — attic inventory — 1939." Source: s-001 (.writer/drafts/s-001.md; .context-builder/history/ch-01/s-001.md).

Lena discovers a folded scrap tamped into a small cedar parcel; in Aunt May's capitals it reads: "sewn into coat." She folds the scrap back into its parcel. Source: s-001 (.writer/drafts/s-001.md; .context-builder/history/ch-01/s-001.md).

Lena uncovers the mirror and observes an anomalous brief lag in her reflection; for a second a child's small hand appears to press from behind the glass: "When I stepped in front of it my reflection lagged by a breath and, for a second, a child's small hand pressed out from behind the glass as if from the other side." Source: s-001 (.writer/drafts/s-001.md; .context-builder/history/ch-01/s-001.md).

Scene includes a folded scrap in a cedar parcel reading 'sewn into coat', suggesting an item (possibly an oval key) may have been sewn into a coat; presence not confirmed by the prose. Source: s-001 (.writer/drafts/s-001.md; .context-builder/history/ch-01/s-001.md).
